title: TypeScript
subtitle: TypeScript builds the meeting-stage app, the relay between Teams and my agent, the public site runtime, and the in-house social integrations.

lede: Auth and access plane includes a product I built to learn what an enterprise agent platform needs from an MCP server: a weather-intelligence server on Express 5 and the official MCP TypeScript SDK. I gave it two surfaces. Desktop assistants get the full set over the local stdio transport; Microsoft Copilot Studio gets a trimmed set over Streamable HTTP, with the session header its connector expects, because that platform copes poorly with large catalogs. I later ported it to C# on the official .NET MCP SDK. Helix needed to live inside the tools people already use. I wrote a Teams admin tab in React and Fluent UI so an administrator manages the digital employee from inside Teams.
quote: Building the same server on two official SDKs showed me which decisions were mine and which were the SDK's.
evidence: MCP server design: a 16,200-line TypeScript weather-intelligence MCP server, the full tool set over stdio and a trimmed set over Streamable HTTP for Copilot Studio.
Event ingestion and idempotency: a 6,500-line vendor event intake that checks signatures over raw bytes, stores before acknowledging and delivers each keyed batch once.
Platform extension without forking: 12,400 lines of TypeScript plugins on an unmodified open-source team chat server.
author: Corey James
